blocks.title: What is this file?
blocks.what: The file starts with the API version and kind. Deployments come from the apps/v1 API.
blocks.why: A Deployment keeps a set number of identical Pods running and replaces any that fail.
blocks.ifRemoved: Kubernetes rejects the file, because it cannot tell what you want to create.
blocks.comment: What to create: a Deployment, from the apps/v1 API

blocks.title: Give it a name
blocks.what: The name is how you find the Deployment later, for example with kubectl get deployment web.
blocks.why: Kubernetes also starts the name of every Pod it creates for this Deployment with web.
blocks.ifRemoved: Kubernetes rejects the file, because every object needs a name.
blocks.comment: A name to find the Deployment
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: web

blocks.title: How many copies?
blocks.what: Replicas is the number of identical Pods to keep running.
blocks.why: If a Pod crashes or its node fails, the Deployment starts a new Pod to get back to this number.
blocks.ifRemoved: Kubernetes uses the default of one replica.
blocks.comment: How many copies of the Pod to keep running
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: web
spec:
  replicas: {{replicas}}

blocks.title: Which Pods belong to it?
blocks.what: The selector tells the Deployment which Pods it manages: the ones labelled app: web.
blocks.why: The Deployment counts and replaces only Pods that match. The next block gives its Pods this label.
blocks.ifRemoved: Kubernetes rejects the file, because apps/v1 Deployments must have a selector.
blocks.comment: Manage the Pods that carry this label
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: web
spec:
  replicas: {{replicas}}
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: web

blocks.title: Describe the Pods
blocks.what: The template is the blueprint for every Pod the Deployment creates. It gives each Pod the label app: web.
blocks.why: The template labels must match the selector, or Kubernetes rejects the Deployment.
blocks.ifRemoved: The Deployment would have nothing to create, so Kubernetes rejects it.
blocks.comment: The blueprint for each Pod, with the label the selector looks for
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: web
spec:
  replicas: {{replicas}}
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: web
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: web

blocks.title: What should run?
blocks.what: Each Pod runs one container from the nginx image, just like in the Pod lesson.
blocks.why: A Pod template needs at least one container. This block makes the file ready to apply.
blocks.ifRemoved: Kubernetes rejects the Deployment, because its Pods would have nothing to run.
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: web
spec:
  replicas: {{replicas}}
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: web
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: web
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: web
          image: nginx:1.30.4

blocks.title: Which port?
blocks.what: This records that each container listens on port 80, where nginx serves its web page.
blocks.why: It tells people and tools which port the app uses. A Service in a later lesson sends traffic here.
blocks.ifRemoved: nginx still listens on port 80, so the Pods work the same. Readers just lose the hint.
blocks.comment: The port the app listens on inside each container
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: web
spec:
  replicas: {{replicas}}
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: web
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: web
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: web
          image: nginx:1.30.4
          ports:
            - containerPort: 80

notes.apiVersion: The API group and version that define this kind. Deployments are in apps/v1.
notes.kind: The type of object to create. A Deployment keeps identical Pods running.
notes.metadata: Details that identify the object, such as its name.
notes.metadata.name: The Deployment's name. Its Pods get names that start with it.
notes.spec: The desired state of the Deployment.
notes.spec.replicas: How many Pods to keep running. The default is 1.
notes.spec.selector: Which Pods this Deployment manages. It cannot change after creation.
notes.spec.selector.matchLabels: Pods must have all of these labels to be managed by this Deployment.
notes.spec.selector.matchLabels.app: Match Pods whose app label is web.
notes.spec.template: The Pod template: the blueprint for every Pod this Deployment creates.
notes.spec.template.metadata: Details given to every Pod created from the template.
notes.spec.template.metadata.labels: Labels given to every Pod. They must match the selector.
notes.spec.template.metadata.labels.app: Every Pod gets the label app: web, so the selector finds it.
notes.spec.template.spec: What each Pod runs. This is the same spec as in a Pod file.
notes.spec.template.spec.containers: The containers in each Pod. Each list item starts with a dash.
notes.spec.template.spec.containers[].name: The container's name. It must be unique within the Pod.
notes.spec.template.spec.containers[].image: The image to run, with a version tag. A fixed tag runs the same version every time.
notes.spec.template.spec.containers[].ports: Ports the container listens on. This list is mostly informational.
The port number the app listens on inside the container.

tryIt.result: One line per replica. Each Pod name starts with web- and shows Running.

tryIt.command: kubectl delete pod <name of one Pod>
tryIt.result: Run kubectl get pods -l app=web again. A new Pod has already replaced it.
Removes the Deployment and all of its Pods.
